newsitem.title: USA: US exporters cannot confirm Egypt cancelled wheat.
newsitem.headline: US exporters cannot confirm Egypt cancelled wheat.

text.p: Several U.S. wheat exporters said they could not confirm a rumor that Egypt cancelled a wheat shipment which sent December wheat futures on Chicago Board of Trade to end sharply lower on Wednesday.
CBOT December wheat closed at $422-1/2 a bushel, down 11-1/4 cents while the rest of the board was off two to 6-3/4 cents.
But one U.S. exporter said Egypt may have cancelled one cargo of optional origin wheat flour. The reasons were not given.
"Many hours ago, they (Egypt) rejected a wheat flour cargo of non-U.S. origin of about 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes," he said.
Another exporter said: "I have just heard the rumours but have not seen any verification of that. I heard they rejected a cargo, that is all I heard."
In August, Egypt posted a limit of two parts per million vomitoxin content for its U.S. purchases of U.S. soft red winter wheat.
Vomitoxin, a toxin produced by fusarium fungus, was reported in various locations of the U.S. soft red winter wheat belt this summer.
Recently, Egypt has been turning to other markets for their needs.
In mid-September, Egypt bought 450,000 tonnes of French soft wheat which sparked a drop in CBOT wheat futures and pushed French wheat prices higher.
